## TL;DR

This task completed a responsive QA pass for Inputs and Context and corrected a request-state bug that made failed list requests look like successful empty results. The first review pass also required captures at both target viewport widths, which were added. Round 2 identified a separate class of bugs: concurrent refreshes could apply stale results or let an old completion overwrite the shared loading/error state. I updated both stores to treat the newest refresh as authoritative and added regression tests for out-of-order successes and superseded failures. The required changed-path check passed after these fixes.

## Work and rationale

I tested Inputs and Repo Context using headless Playwright Chromium against the auth-less development server started from this task worktree. I checked the pages at 1280 and 375 CSS pixels, including Inputs list and board modes, an input detail drawer, the New input screenshot picker and preview, and the Docs, Skills, Discover, and History tabs. I selected a small image, confirmed its preview, then removed it without submitting a new input. Existing document content rendered in the Context tree and preview. The tested pages stayed within the viewport at both widths.

I also exercised API failure states by returning 503 for listing requests. Inputs initially had no way to distinguish “the request failed” from “there are no inputs,” because the store swallowed the error while retaining its empty initial list. Context similarly showed an empty Docs result while loading or after a failed request. I changed Inputs refresh to report success and failure so the view can show a retryable error instead of a misleading empty state. The docs store now exposes loading and error state, and Context renders the true empty message only after a successful empty response. Playwright confirmed both Retry actions recover after the APIs are allowed through.

The review identified another race in those refresh paths. App startup and the Context refresh control can call `loadDocs()` concurrently. Previously any completion could change `docsLoading` or `docsLoadError`, and an older response could replace the newer listing. The Inputs page and background enrichment paths can similarly overlap `refreshInputs()`. I added monotonically increasing request versions in both stores. Only the latest request can update shared data and request state; stale responses are ignored. A superseded failure is treated as an obsolete result by its caller, so it does not report a stale error after a more recent refresh has taken over.

The QA note now records the request ordering rule and its regression coverage alongside the responsive and failure-state observations. Review captures were declared for Inputs and Context at desktop and phone dimensions, with routes matching the pages under test.

## Approaches tried

For the responsive pass, I used the auth-less server in this task worktree and headless Playwright, checking viewport scroll width and exercising the actual picker and preview controls. For the failure cases, I intercepted all matching list requests and held them at 503 until Retry was selected. This avoided a second startup or background request clearing the failure before it could be observed.

For the concurrency fix, I used deferred promises to control completion order. The docs tests verify that an older success cannot clear loading while a newer request remains pending, that the new response remains in the store when the old response later finishes, and that a stale failure does not replace a later success or leave an error behind. The Inputs tests similarly resolve the newer response first and then finish the older success or failure; the newer snapshot remains in the store and a superseded failure is not reported as current. The repository test wrapper also runs the boot-timing suite, which passed with the focused tests.

## Challenges and blockers

I first exercised the pages with their normal data and then simulated service failures separately. The first failure probe allowed a background refresh to succeed before the error assertion, so it was not deterministic; I changed the interception to keep all matching requests failing until the explicit retry. During the review fix, I considered relying only on request completion order, but that leaves loading and error flags vulnerable even if list data is protected. The version guard therefore covers both shared request state and the data assignment, and the tests explicitly hold the later request pending while the earlier one completes.

The first browser failure probe exposed a test setup race rather than a product blocker: a second request could recover while the assertion was waiting. Controlling every matching request made that path repeatable. The concurrency issue was reproducible with controlled promises and did not require a real server failure or a timing-based test. The remote changed-path check takes several minutes but completed successfully. No external account or device was required, and no source changes were needed after the passing check.

## Key learnings

An empty state is trustworthy only after a successful response. Loading, failure, and successful emptiness need separate representations so a request error cannot appear as an empty project. For concurrent refreshes, list data and request state must share the same authority rule. Ignoring stale data alone is not enough: an old `finally` can hide a still-running request, and an old `catch` can resurrect an error after a later success. A request version lets each completion update shared state only while it remains current.

The targeted regression tests passed, including their boot-timing wrapper suite. The UI build and typecheck passed. `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` then passed formatting, lint, build, CSS and theme guards, rendered contrast, branch artifact and task-asset checks, remote changed-path tests, and UI smoke. The prior browser pass used headless Chromium only; no visible browser window was opened.
